note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  ~2 months of low energy/fatigue, difficulty getting up, insomnia, reduced appetite, poor concentration/distractibility, lower mood, decreased sex drive; new exertional shortness of breath during sports; onset temporally associated with starting a new job ~2 months ago; known hypothyroidism on Thyroxine. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. No vision changes.
- Relevant family medical history:  Father died by suicide (~15 years ago). Mother well. Only child. No other family psychiatric or medical history reported.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Thyroxine (levothyroxine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Married; decreased libido over the past few months. Morning erections: initially reported not noticing them recently, later stated no change (conflict noted).
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Participates in sports; reports reduced appetite; reports new shortness of breath during sports.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Lower mood; insomnia; fatigue; impaired concentration; denies suicidal or homicidal thoughts. Family history of suicide (father).
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Denies vision changes.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Married; started a new job ~2 months ago. Only child. Caring responsibilities not recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not applicable (male) / Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not applicable / Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Subacute (≈2 months) fatigue, insomnia, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, lower mood, decreased libido, and new exertional dyspnea. Known hypothyroidism on Thyroxine (dose unknown). Denies suicidal ideation. No visual changes. Stressor: new job coinciding with symptom onset.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript):
  - Major depressive disorder vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood (High): Low mood, insomnia, low energy, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, decreased libido; temporally linked to job change; still some enjoyment at times; no suicidality.
  - Thyroid dysfunction related to hypothyroidism/levothyroxine dosing (Medium): History of hypothyroidism; symptoms could reflect under-replacement (fatigue, low mood, low libido) or over-replacement (insomnia, exertional dyspnea). Requires TSH/free T4.
  - Anemia (Medium): Fatigue and exertional dyspnea; decreased appetite. Needs CBC and iron studies.
  - Primary insomnia/stress-related sleep disturbance (contributing) (Medium): Difficulty sleeping since job change could exacerbate fatigue and mood symptoms.
  - Hypogonadism (Low–Medium): Decreased libido; morning erection history conflicted.
- Working diagnosis: Undifferentiated fatigue with mood symptoms and exertional dyspnea; likely multifactorial—possible adjustment-related depression/anxiety with need to exclude thyroid dysfunction and anemia.
- Management priorities: In-person assessment with physical exam and targeted labs; screen mood formally; assess cardiopulmonary status for dyspnea; review levothyroxine adherence and dosing.

Management Plan

- Actions/recommendations provided:
  - Patient to book an in-person appointment with GP in the next few days for physical examination and blood tests.
- Additional considerations to discuss/arrange at in-person visit (based on presentation and DDx; not yet performed):
  - Labs: TSH and free T4; CBC with indices; ferritin and iron studies; vitamin B12 and folate; vitamin D; fasting glucose and lipid panel; consider morning total testosterone if low libido persists after addressing mood/thyroid.
  - Review levothyroxine adherence, timing with meals/meds, and recent dose changes.
  - Mental health screening: PHQ-9 and GAD-7; safety assessment to be revisited.
  - Dyspnea evaluation: Vitals, pulse oximetry, cardiopulmonary exam; consider ECG if indicated based on exam/history.
- Safety: Patient currently denies suicidal ideation; continue to monitor at follow-up.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Major depressive disorder vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood — High likelihood: Low mood, insomnia, reduced appetite, poor concentration, decreased libido, temporal association with new job.
- Thyroid dysfunction (under/over-replacement of levothyroxine) — Moderate likelihood: Known hypothyroidism on Thyroxine; symptoms span both potential under- and over-replacement; requires TSH/free T4.
- Anemia (iron deficiency or other) — Moderate likelihood: Fatigue and exertional dyspnea; decreased appetite; needs CBC and iron studies.

Quality checks

- Missing/expected elements: Indigenous status; vitals (BP, pulse), height/weight/BMI/waist; cardiovascular and respiratory exam; oral/ear/vision screening; urinalysis; immunization review; alcohol/tobacco/substance use history; detailed diet and physical activity; full sexual health history; sleep hygiene; preventive care status.
- Internal contradictions: Morning erections initially reported as not noticed recently, later stated no change (conflict noted). Brief confusion in conversation between “hyperthyroid” vs “hypothyroid,” ultimately clarified as hypothyroidism.
- Transcript quality: Occasional pauses/freeze and minor miscommunication; overall content adequate to outline primary concerns and plan.
